students.summary: S1 defined speed and velocity correctly and worked out average speed for a two-part journey without help. Needed a hint to explain why velocity can be zero when distance is not.
strong_points: Calculates average speed for a journey
areas_of_improvement: Why displacement can be zero after a round trip
next_steps: Trace a round trip on paper and mark start and end points

students.summary: S2 defined speed well but used speed and velocity as the same thing until prompted. Unit conversion from km/h to m/s was shaky.
areas_of_improvement: Treats velocity as the same as speed
next_steps: Practise converting three everyday speeds to m/s

students.summary: S3 recalled the formula for speed but could not explain what it means. Did not know that velocity has a direction, and could not describe acceleration.
areas_of_improvement: Explaining the speed formula in words
next_steps: Describe a walk to school with distance, time and direction

students.summary: S4 explained uniform and non-uniform motion with good examples. Mixed up distance and displacement for a circular track.
strong_points: Explains uniform and non-uniform motion with examples
areas_of_improvement: Displacement on a circular track after one lap

students.summary: S5 knew speed is distance over time. Said velocity and speed are the same and struggled to convert km/h to m/s.
strong_points: Knows speed is distance over time
areas_of_improvement: Velocity is speed with a direction
next_steps: Practise unit conversion with a simple table
